decisions.reason: The Definition falsely asserts that infinite intensity forces an arbitrary point-process count to be infinite almost surely. On the discrete positive integers, let P(N=n)=1/[n(n+1)] for n>=1 and eta=sum_{j=1}^N delta_j. These probabilities telescope to one; every configuration is finite and measurable, while nu({j})=P(N>=j)=1/j and nu(S)=sum_j 1/j=infinity. Thus eta(S)=N is finite almost surely even with locally finite intensity. Restricting the convention to Poisson point-process counts repairs this false mathematical assertion.
